I don't know if this counts as it's less cooking, more assembling... But regardless, I have two sandwiches that are like heaven for me:

Sandwich Numero Uno:

Step one: Go to store and acquire:

  • A nice fucking bun. Don't be cheap - It's like $0.30 for a lame bun vs $0.60 for something like this.
  • Spicy turkey breast from the deli counter - Tuscan or something that sounds awesome like that. Don't get that prepackaged shit that's covered in slimy-ass preservatives. Shaved.
  • Swiss cheese
  • Bacon. Good, honest, real bacon. No "Canadian Bacon" or "I-wish-I-was-Canadian-maple-bacon bacon". Smoked or something like that is what you want.
  • Lettuce
  • A cucumber
  • A green pepper
  • Italian salad dressing - the kraft one is dope.
  • Olives (sliced pizza style) are optional.

Fry that bacon up. Right crispy, as is the bacon-master-race way (don't burn it though...). Two pieces of it. While the bacon is being fried, wash your veggies, and slice the cucumber and pepper, small-ish.

Now slice the bun in half, hot dog style. Put a layer of swiss cheese on both sides of it, and pop her in the oven (toaster oven is okay I guess) on broil for like a minute until the cheese is melted.

Take your turkey and lay it nicely on the bottom half of your bun. I usually go for 4 slices and that gives a nice turkey-to-restofsandwich ratio. Pop her back into the oven to warm that bird meat up.

Take your sandwich, put your veggies on top of the now-warm turkey. Lettuce, peppers, cucumbers (olives if your feeling them), in that order. It helps to ensure sandwich stability. Bacon on top of all that. a squeeze or two of italian dressing on top and you're almost done.

All that's left is that ninja knife trick thing they do at subway to magically make everything fit perfectly within the bun, slice that puppy in half too, and you're done!

Sandwich Numero... Two (???):

What's needed:

  • Similar bun to above. This shit is important.
  • Roast beef. Again, none of that slimy preservative-filled, prepackaged shit. If you're going to do it, do it right.
  • Swiss cheese - the king of cheeses
  • Butter
  • Garlic
  • Steak Spice The "Club House - La Grille" is pretty good. There' also a "The Keg" branded one that is far superior, but harder to find.

Slice that bun in half, hot-dog style of course.

Crush some garlic. Mix in with butter. If your butter is hard, microwave it for like 10-15 seconds.

Butter both sides of bun and place a layer of cheese on each. Put it in the oven on broil for a minute or two to make it all toasty and melty. When it's toasted, lay a few slices of roast beef on there and put it back in to get nice and warm.

Take it out, throw on some of that steak spice, reassemble into sandwich (opposed to like open-faced), eat.

I love to make my own chicken stock. It's easy and is great for broth and making homemade chicken soup. From one chicken I can get what would equal three boxed chicken stock at the store.

Take all the remaining tidbits of a grocery store rotisserie chicken and put it in a crock pot or big stock pot. Throw in an onion, some fresh garlic, and water. Cook for 3-5 hours. I'll put my crockpot on before I go to bed, let it cook all night.

After it cooks strain out all the bits. I will dig through and pick out chicken pieces left over and put those pieces in one of the containers. That will be my chicken soup base. The rest is straight broth I use for cooking.

To make the soup: reheat your soup base. Add Rosemary, sage, thyme, salt and pepper, whatever other spices to your pleasing. Add in pasta of choice (egg noodles, rice, pearl pasta). Simmer until noodles are tender. Done! Ten minutes, best soup you will ever have.

This is probably my favorite. Translation below

  • 200grams of ground pork - or any meat really, I use cubed chicken
  • 1 onion
  • 1 block of tofu - Softest is preferred, but any is fine
  • 2 tsp of garlic - My chili paste is garlic chili paste so I only add 1 tsp or just none
  • 1 tsp of ginger - I just put a ginger tea bag in after I put in the water and take it out before serving
  • ~1/2 tbsp of chili paste - I use 1tbsp of this
  • 2 tbsp each of soy sauce, sake, sugar, and sweet flour paste - I can't get the sweet flour paste where I live so I just leave it out. You can apparently use 2tbsp of miso instead but as I don't have miso around here either I haven't tried it. Replace sake with wine if you want.
  • 600 ml of water
  • 2tbsp of chicken granules - you can replace the water with chicken stock to leave this out

To make the soup thicker mix up to 2tbsp each of water and corn starch. Add at the end as you prefer.

How to make:

  1. Cut onion

  2. Heat oil in frying pan, saute meat. When the meat changes color add onions. - I remove the meat and place it in a bowl to be added at the end to prevent overcooking, but if you're lazy it's okay to leave it in.

  3. When the onion starts getting transparent add garlic, ginger, chili paste. Stir.

  4. Add sweet flour paste, soy sauce, sake, sugar. Stir.

  5. Add water and chicken granules, lightly boil for 5 minutes.

  6. While waiting, taste test the stock. Add more ingredients to your preference (sugar, wine, etc).

  7. Dice tofu, add. Simmer for 5 minutes. If lazy add whole block in and smush with whatever you're stirring with.

  8. Add corn starch as you prefer while stirring gently. Done.
